transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-11-03
Start time: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Priya Agarwal (CTO - Lumina HealthTech), Carlos Mendes (ML Eng), Ellen Park (Security Arch), Samir Rao (Product), Jinsoo Lee (Infra)
Links shared: slide deck (https://redwood.app/decks/lumina-intro), benchmark template (https://redwood.app/benchmarks/lumina-2025), security pack placeholder (link to S3)

Summary:
- Intro/discovery for model selection: open models vs small proprietary, 32k+ context requirement, multilingual support (EN/ES/FR/KO), and tool-calling for EHR fetches and knowledge DBs.
- Customer leaning toward a Dedicated or Private deployment because of PHI concerns but wants to evaluate hosted performance/cost first.
- Action items: pricing spreadsheet, perf benchmarks, security requirements doc, pilot planning.

Topics:
1) Current infra and constraints
2) Context length and retrieval/tool-calling patterns
3) Open-model tradeoffs (quantization, latency, hallucinations)
4) Deployment options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
5) Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs)
6) Next steps / pilot scope

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription may contain small errors):
00:00 Maya Chen: All right hi everyone thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood Inference, joining with Liam our SE. How's everybody today?
00:12 Priya Agarwal: Hi Maya, hi Liam. Good, thanks. We just want to move quickly, we have an internal timeline to pick a vendor by end of year.
00:20 Maya Chen: Great, that's useful context. Quick round robin and then we'll dig into the workload.
00:30 Carlos Mendes: Carlos here — ML Eng. We're mainly building clinician assist features and a triage QA bot, dealing with PHI-ish metadata.
00:38 Ellen Park: Ellen, security arch. We'll need to understand encryption, K M S integration, audit trails, and whether data ever leaves our VPC.
00:46 Liam O'Connor: Thanks Ellen. Just to flag, Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private — different tradeoffs. We'll cover performance and security options.
00:54 Samir Rao: Samir, product. Important for us: multilingual responses (English, Spanish, French, Korean) and consistent outputs across languages.
01:05 Jinsoo Lee: Jinsoo infra — questions around VPC peering, egress, and tenancy models.
01:10 Maya Chen: Perfect. Priya you said vendor decision by EOY — what's the hard timeline for a pilot?
01:18 Priya Agarwal: Ideally a pilot in early December, maybe 2-4 weeks to evaluate. Budget set for a PoC.
01:24 Maya Chen: Good. Can you describe the prompts and context length you're expecting?
01:30 Carlos Mendes: Typical prompt with patient notes + recent visit history, sometimes long context of 10k to 30k tokens, we do retrieval over documents, and we need to keep long trails for summarization. So 32k would be ideal.
01:46 Liam O'Connor: Understood. We can run models that support 32k context — both some open models and our optimized variants. There's tradeoffs with latency/cost at those lengths.
01:58 Priya Agarwal: Also curious about tool-calling — we want model to call internal APIs to fetch EHR snippets and then synthesize. How does that work with Redwood?
02:08 Liam O'Connor: We support tool-calling pattern — it's primarily an application-side orchestration but Redwood supports structured outputs, function-calling style, and streaming. For private deployments you can keep the EHR calls within your network.
02:23 Ellen Park: Important: any offload of KV cache or prefix caching — where does that live? Is it encrypted at rest and in our tenancy?
02:33 Liam O'Connor: Cache lives on the serving nodes. For dedicated/private we can configure encryption at rest and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). For hosted, we offer managed encryption but can restrict retention.
02:44 Priya Agarwal: What about open models vs Anthropic/GPT — we're leaning toward open for cost but worried about hallucinations and safety.
02:54 Maya Chen: Good question. Open models (like Llama2 variants, Mistral-ish families, newer hybrids) can be heavily tuned and quantized for cost but you'll often need an eval loop + guardrails. We usually recommend a mixed approach: start hosted with a vetted open model, run safety/eval, then move to Dedicated if latency or tenancy issues arise.
03:15 Carlos Mendes: Do you have examples of latency at 32k tokens? Even ballpark numbers?
03:22 Liam O'Connor: Roughly speaking, end-to-end token generation latency scales non-linearly with context. For a 32k context with a 7B-class open model on Dedicated optimized runtime, you might see X to Y seconds per 1k tokens — (note: verbal estimate, we'll run exact numbers). We'll send a benchmark.
03:40 Priya Agarwal: We need cost per session estimates too — to compare hosted vs dedicated.
03:46 Maya Chen: We'll share the hosted vs dedicated pricing sheet. Hosted is simpler but higher per-token; Dedicated has base reserved costs but lower unit price for sustained throughput.
03:55 Samir Rao: Multilingual model consistency — are the open models trained enough on Korean/French? We had weird outputs in Spanish previously.
04:05 Liam O'Connor: Some open models are stronger in European languages; Korean can vary. We can include a multilingual eval in the benchmark — pass your prompt set in each language to check regressions.
04:19 Carlos Mendes: For tool-calling, how do you handle latency when model waits for external API responses? Any async patterns?
04:27 Liam O'Connor: Common pattern: call model to decide tools, orchestrate API calls asynchronously, then stitch the results back into a follow-up request. Redwood's streaming and function-calling support is designed for that; we also support a responder pattern to reduce idle GPU time.
04:44 Ellen Park: On the security side, we have three must-haves: SOC2 Type II or equivalent, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs for every request including user id.
04:55 Maya Chen: Noted. Redwood has SOC 2, and we support CMK integration for Dedicated/Private. Audit logs are available in Redwood Console — token-level traces, route and model metadata. We'll share the security pack.
05:10 Jinsoo Lee: For Private deployments, what's the packaging? Is it air-gapped appliance or do you need a control plane connection?
05:17 Liam O'Connor: Private can be fully air-gapped or hybrid. The default private model is a customer-controlled control plane with optional telemetry. For fully air-gapped we provide an on-prem package and offline upgrade artifacts. We'll detail options.
05:30 Priya Agarwal: If we start hosted for speed, can we later migrate the pinned model to Dedicated without retraining?
05:37 Maya Chen: Yes — one of Redwood's key features is consistent deployment abstraction. You can pin model versions and move them across hosted/dedicated/private; runtime differences are managed by our tooling.
05:47 Carlos Mendes: About quantization — we need to know if 8-bit/4-bit quantization impacts retrieval-augmented generation accuracy.
05:55 Liam O'Connor: It can, depending on model and workload. We'll include quantization profiles and recommended models in the benchmark. Sometimes you lose subtle factuality at aggressive quant levels, especially for long-context RAG.
06:08 Samir Rao: Any restrictions on custom fine-tuning? We might want to do some supervised fine-tuning on clinical notes.
06:15 Maya Chen: We support fine-tuning workflows for Dedicated/private customers. For hosted we have limited fine-tuning options and advise on RLHF style approaches; we'll clarify in the doc.
06:25 Priya Agarwal: Are there customers in healthcare already using Redwood? Any referenceable case studies?
06:30 Maya Chen: We have several anonymized references in healthcare and a checklist for PHI handling. We'll share that and can arrange references after an NDA if needed.
06:45 Carlos Mendes: On benchmarking, we want to compare three open models (A, B, C) plus Anthropic small and GPT-like baseline. Can Redwood run these side-by-side on the same infrastructure?
06:55 Liam O'Connor: Yes — we can provision benchmark runs and produce token-level latency, cost, and hallucination metrics. We'll also include the effect of kv cache/prefix caching and batch sizing.
07:08 Ellen Park: How long do logs persist in hosted vs dedicated? Retention and the ability to purge are important for compliance.
07:16 Maya Chen: Hosted has configurable retention windows; Dedicated gives you control to set retention and purge policies, and Private puts everything in your storage so you control retention. We'll include retention options in the security pack.
07:30 Priya Agarwal: Okay let's talk about a pilot scope. We're thinking: 2-week hosted pilot with our prompt set, then if results look good a 4-week dedicated eval for sustained throughput. Is that a reasonable path?
07:42 Maya Chen: That path is common and reasonable. Pilot goals should include latency targets, cost per session, hallucination rate below X% (you define threshold), and tool-calling reliability.
07:53 Carlos Mendes: One technical note: our retrieval system returns ~15 documents on average and we often append full docs to context — can we use prefix caching instead?
08:02 Liam O'Connor: Yes, prefix/KV caching is a common optimization to avoid re-sending full docs; Redwood supports KV caches and will cache repeated prefixes for faster generation.
08:12 Samir Rao: Any gotchas with streaming when using tool-calling and partial outputs?
08:18 Liam O'Connor: Streaming works; when the model calls a tool you'll see a structured intermediate and you can stream partial outputs. We recommend an orchestration layer to handle partial tool responses and stitching.
08:30 Priya Agarwal: Pricing question: how do you bill for context tokens vs generated tokens?
08:36 Maya Chen: Hosted billing breaks down input vs output tokens; Dedicated you negotiate unit pricing and the cost model is per-token plus reserved capacity. We'll show examples in the sheet.
08:48 Ellen Park: For CMK integration, do you support HSM keys from AWS CloudHSM or bring-your-own?
08:54 Liam O'Connor: For Dedicated/Private we support BYOK with standard HSM integrations; hosted can integrate with a partner-managed KMS but for full BYOK you likely go Dedicated/Private.
09:05 Carlos Mendes: Do you offer model eval tooling out of the box? We need a regression alerting tied to prompt sets.
09:12 Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood Optimize includes eval harnesses and quality monitoring; you can attach prompt sets and get regression alerts and diffs. We'll include a demo in the follow-up.
09:24 Samir Rao: Any limits on total context length if we chain tool calls? Like multiple round trips?
09:30 Liam O'Connor: The runtime supports continuous batching and KV cache — chain length depends on sequence length budget. For multi-turn tool-heavy flows we recommend session management and cache usage to avoid blowing past token limits.
09:45 Priya Agarwal: Regulatory question — do you do data residency guarantees? We operate in EU for some patients.
09:52 Maya Chen: We have region controls and Private deployments can be fully in-customer region. Hosted has region choices but if you need strict residency we recommend Dedicated/Private.
10:05 Carlos Mendes: Any recommended open models for 32k long-context and multilingual strength?
10:12 Liam O'Connor: A few LLM families are emerging with extended context; some Mistral-Like and Falcon derivatives have better long context variants. We'll propose 2-3 models in our benchmark: one cost-optimized quantized 8-bit model, one accuracy-focused 16-bit model, and one multilingual-tuned variant.
10:32 Maya Chen: Quick note — we'll run a 32k context bench and a multilingual pass across EN/ES/FR/KO and include tool-calling scenarios. Liam will run this and share results.
10:45 Priya Agarwal: Sounds good. One last question: SLA expectations for Dedicated? We need 99.95% uptime and latency SLOs.
10:52 Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA options and configurable autoscaling policies to meet latency targets; we'll include typical SLA language and options.
11:05 Ellen Park: Also need clarity on data access controls and RBAC in the console.
11:12 Liam O'Connor: Redwood Console supports role-based access and token scoping; you'll be able to restrict operations by team and route.
11:25 Maya Chen: Great — recap: Maya will share deck and pricing sheet, Liam will run benchmarks, Ellen will send security checklist, Carlos will provide prompt set. We'll target the pilot start in early December.
11:40 Priya Agarwal: Thanks everyone. We'll review the materials and schedule the infra deep-dive.
11:48 Maya Chen: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites and the docs.

End of transcript
